traceability.evidence:
Implementation: - Core rule: src/rules/valid-annotation-format.ts - Options helper: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts - Error-message helper: src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-utils.ts - Related integration rule: src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts
Configuration & behavior: - AnnotationRuleOptions includes flat options: storyPathPattern, storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern, requirementIdExample, plus nested story.pattern/example and req.pattern/example (src/rules/helpers/valid-annotation-options.ts). - resolveOptions() normalizes raw ESLint options, handling nested and flat forms and producing ResolvedAnnotationOptions with storyPattern, storyExample, reqPattern, reqExample. - resolvePattern() validates regex strings (nested first, then flat). On invalid regex, it records a stable error message via buildInvalidRegexError() and returns default patterns, ensuring fallback behavior. - resolveExample() prefers nested example, then flat example, then defaults, feeding into buildStoryErrorMessage() and buildReqErrorMessage() so error messages can use custom examples. - getRuleSchema() returns a JSON schema object used as meta.schema for valid-annotation-format, with properties for story/req objects and the flat shorthand fields, and additionalProperties: false. - valid-annotation-format.ts uses: - meta.schema = getRuleSchema(). - meta.messages.invalidRuleConfiguration tied to this story’s regex-validation/backward-compat requirements. - create(): calls resolveOptions(), then reads getOptionErrors() and reports each with messageId "invalidRuleConfiguration". - validateStoryAnnotation()/validateReqAnnotation() use options.storyPattern and options.reqPattern, so configured patterns take effect and defaults apply when not configured. - buildStoryErrorMessage()/buildReqErrorMessage() use options.storyExample/reqExample (falling back to defaults), enabling custom examples in diagnostics.
Tests: - tests/rules/valid-annotation-format.test.ts header explicitly references this story: - "Tests for: docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md" - @story docs/stories/010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS.story.md - Tests cover: - Nested configuration: custom story.pattern and req.pattern with corresponding examples (valid cases like [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH]). - Flat configuration: storyPathPattern/storyPathExample and requirementIdPattern/requirementIdExample (valid cases [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-STORY-FLAT], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-REQ-FLAT], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-BOTH-FLAT]). - Custom examples in messages: tests explicitly assert the exact error strings where custom story/req examples appear. - Invalid regex patterns (nested and flat): tests expect both invalidRuleConfiguration errors with precise field names and continued use of default patterns for actual validation (e.g. [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK], [REQ-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS-FALLBACK-FLAT]). - Precedence rules: tests verify nested story/req.pattern and nested examples override flat shorthand values ([REQ-PATTERN-CONFIG], [REQ-EXAMPLE-MESSAGES]).
Documentation: - docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md documents: - Nested configuration (story.pattern/story.example, req.pattern/req.example) with defaults matching the implementation. - Flat shorthand (storyPathPattern/storyPathExample, requirementIdPattern/requirementIdExample) and their mapping to nested fields. - Behavior on invalid regex: reports invalidRuleConfiguration and falls back to default patterns.
Integration consistency: - valid-story-reference.ts uses defaultStoryDirs = ["docs/stories", "stories"], matching valid-annotation-format’s default story pattern rooted at "docs/stories". Both rules can be configured independently yet consistently (custom directories plus custom patterns).
traceability.notes: All acceptance criteria for 010.1-DEV-CONFIGURABLE-PATTERNS are implemented and verified. The rule supports configurable story and requirement ID patterns via both nested and flat options, validates regex strings with clear configuration errors and safe fallbacks, uses configurable examples in error messages, exposes a proper JSON schema, and aligns defaults with valid-story-reference. Tests explicitly tied to this story cover valid/invalid configuration, precedence between nested and flat options, custom example text, and fallback behavior. Documentation in docs/rules/valid-annotation-format.md explains configuration and behavior, matching the implemented code. No unmet acceptance criteria were found.
